definitions.position: Raw common-initialization odom-frame position difference at exactly matched scan timestamps. No trajectory fitting or scale alignment.
definitions.orientation: SO(3) geodesic angle of relative rotation.
definitions.runtime: steady_clock duration of original MapBuilder::process including common diagnostics; excludes bag decoding, input scaling, ROS transport, publication and controller.
definitions.plane_rms: Point-to-own-map plane residual RMS at last evaluated update linearization. Internal consistency only; map and selected correspondences vary with variant.
definitions.gravity_difference: Difference in body-frame projection of the same fixed world gravity. Sensitivity proxy for downstream gravity removal, not physical attitude error.
definitions.lap_gap: 3D distance between estimated positions interpolated at original MPCC diagnostic lap boundaries. Contains actual path/phase variation, not pure odometry drift.

recorded_lio_agreement.limitation: Recorded LIO is a shared-sensor baseline, not accuracy truth; live startup predates recorded raw IMU and cannot be reproduced from missing input.

limitations: No independent trajectory, attitude or ground-speed truth; smaller version difference or smaller bias is not proof of better accuracy.
Full sensor bag is read, but recorded raw IMU starts later than LiDAR/LIO; 14 pre-coverage scans cannot propagate. Startup is reinitialized from available data.
All variants process exactly the same 2220 scan packages without scheduling-related frame dropping; this is core replay, not original live callback timing.
Desktop AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, isolated Docker, 4 CPU quota, 2 OpenMP threads. Timing does not qualify NX timing.
Point-to-own-map residuals and lap endpoint gaps are internal/consistency metrics, not independent accuracy measurements.
Three timing repetitions for x10/x9.81 and one for other policies; distribution across frames is not a confidence interval.
Static normalization uses 26 initial available IMU samples; initialization assumes stationarity and cannot separate bias from scale.
